explanation: Think of surveillance as keeping a close eye on community health trends. By gathering data continually, nurses and health planners can spot issues early and plan the right actions to keep everyone safe and well! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h1)

question: Which virus is notorious for surviving on medical equipment and surfaces for days, making it very easy to spread if equipment is reused?

options.A: Influenza Virus
options.B: Streptococcus Pneumoniae
options.C: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.D: Hepatitis B Virus

explanation: Hepatitis B is a tough survivor and can live on surfaces and tools outside the body for days. That's why strict sterilization and single-use rules are non-negotiable. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T2#GNS122_U3_T2_h3)

question: How do sheltered workshops differ from regular commercial workplaces?

options.A: They focus exclusively on manufacturing heavy machinery
options.B: They require employees to work without any supervision
options.C: They pay workers much higher wages than regular jobs
options.D: They modify production demands and lower output pressure

explanation: Because workers may have disabilities, these workshops adjust workloads and reduce stress to match what each individual can comfortably handle. Great job thinking this through! [learn more](GNS314_U5_T7#GNS314_U5_T7_h1)

question: Why does the brain cut back on its own chemical receptors after repeated drug use?

options.A: To increase the speed of normal digestion
options.B: To store extra energy for physical exercise
options.C: To improve overall visual acuity at night
options.D: To protect itself from chemical overload

explanation: Well thought out! When a drug floods the brain, it tries to protect itself by reducing receptors (down-regulation) to restore some balance. The body is always trying to keep things stable! [learn more](GNS223_U6_T5#GNS223_U6_T5_h2)

question: What is the difference between monitoring and evaluation?

options.A: Monitoring is done by the government, while evaluation is done by children
options.B: Monitoring costs money, while evaluation is completely free
options.C: Monitoring happens continuously during the project, while evaluation measures final results
options.D: Monitoring focuses on drugs, while evaluation focuses on buildings

explanation: Monitoring tracks progress day-by-day, whereas evaluation looks back at the end to see if the main goals were met. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h7)

question: What behavior might you notice in a patient who has reached acceptance?

options.A: Conserving energy and withdrawing into quiet reflection
options.B: Arguing with family over small things
options.C: Demanding aggressive new experimental treatments
options.D: Denying that they have any symptoms at all

explanation: As energy fades, patients in acceptance often quiet down, letting go of worldly fuss to rest in peace. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T3#GNS221_U4_T3_h6)

question: In Nigerian public health, what does the acronym IDSR stand for?

options.A: Infectious Disease Sanitation Routine
options.B: Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response
options.C: Immediate District Symptom Record
options.D: International Drug Safety Regulation

explanation: Correct! IDSR is the helpful framework our health facilities use to track, report, and respond to important diseases efficiently. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T15#GNS313_U1_T15_h6)

question: If you are talking to local village elders about building a new maternity clinic, how should you pitch it?

options.A: Discuss advanced surgical techniques used in teaching hospitals
options.B: Focus on family health, community safety, and local traditions
options.C: Present complex statistical models on maternal mortality ratios
options.D: Emphasize strict government legal codes and budget allocations

explanation: You're doing great! Village elders want to hear about real, practical things that protect and respect their families and community traditions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T8#GNS124_U4_T8_h2)

question: A stable patient complains that monthly clinic visits for pill refills make them miss work and spend too much on transport. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: Require the patient to come to the clinic twice a week instead
options.B: Scold the patient for not prioritizing clinic visits over their job
options.C: Enroll the patient in a multi-month dispensing program if they are stable
options.D: Tell the patient they can stop taking their medication entirely

explanation: Brilliant! Multi-month dispensing gives stable patients several months of drugs at once, saving them transport money and protecting their daily work life. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T4#GNS216_U6_T4_h8)

question: Which category of workplace hazard includes exposure to loud machinery noise and extreme heat?

options.A: Physical hazards
options.B: Chemical hazards
options.C: Psychosocial hazards
options.D: Biological hazards

explanation: Noise, vibration, radiation, and extreme temperatures are classified as physical workplace hazards. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h4)

question: What tip should a nurse give a pregnant woman to help prevent severe morning nausea?

options.A: Drink a large glass of orange juice immediately upon waking up
options.B: Skip breakfast entirely until the afternoon hours arrive
options.C: Keep plain crackers near the bed and eat a small amount before getting up
options.D: Exercise vigorously for twenty minutes before eating breakfast

explanation: Nibbling a dry cracker before getting out of bed lifts morning blood sugar and settles an empty stomach. Classic nursing advice that really helps patients! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h8)

question: Which lab value usually climbs when a patient has failing kidneys and can't clear protein waste?

options.A: Serum potassium levels
options.B: Red blood cell count
options.C: Blood urea nitrogen
options.D: Total body water weight

explanation: Since urea is the main waste product of protein, sluggish kidneys mean urea backs up, causing Blood Urea Nitrogen (BUN) levels to rise. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T010#GNS227_U1_T010_h6)

question: What does 'leadership disconnect' mean in healthcare management?

options.A: Physicians failing to document patient progress notes on time
options.B: The hospital losing its internet and electronic health record connection
options.C: Executives making decisions without understanding frontline clinical realities
options.D: Nurses refusing to speak with doctors during emergency situations

explanation: Spot on! Disconnect happens when managers sitting far away in offices make policies that just don't match the everyday realities of the ward. [learn more](GST319_U6_T7#GST319_U6_T7_h6)

question: What causes painful breast engorgement when a baby misses feeds?

options.A: Sudden permanent damage to the myoepithelial cells
options.B: Accumulation of milk and fluid buildup in the alveoli
options.C: A rapid increase in maternal estrogen levels
options.D: An excessive surge of oxytocin from the posterior pituitary

explanation: Correct! When milk isn't removed, it backs up and causes pressure, swelling, and tenderness in the breast tissue. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T18#GNS121_U5_T18_h6)

question: Which standardized nursing terminology is used specifically to name clinical nursing diagnoses?

options.A: NANDA-I
options.B: NIC
options.C: NOC
options.D: ICD-10

explanation: Great nursing care starts with clear language! NANDA-I gives us the official framework for naming the human responses and health issues we diagnose and treat every day. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h2)

question: A nurse manager wants to track patient fall rates over the last six months. What should be placed on the horizontal X-axis?

options.A: The total number of patient falls
options.B: The time intervals like months
options.C: The median value of the data
options.D: The names of the injured patients

explanation: The horizontal X-axis is always reserved for the time sequence, such as days, weeks, or months. [learn more](GST319_U1_T3#GST319_U1_T3_h3)

question: How is a wheat allergy different from celiac disease?

options.A: Wheat allergy involves IgE antibody responses rather than autoimmune villous atrophy
options.B: Celiac disease symptoms only appear after age fifty
options.C: Wheat allergy causes permanent damage to the liver instead of the gut
options.D: Celiac disease is caused by a bacterial infection of the stomach

explanation: A wheat allergy is a classic immune system allergic reaction (using IgE antibodies), whereas celiac disease is an autoimmune condition that specifically harms the gut lining. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T011#GNS227_U6_T011_h2)

question: Why are digital health records generally safer than traditional paper notes?

options.A: They allow patients to change their own treatment plans online
options.B: They remove the need for nurses to document care procedures
options.C: They are completely immune to technical errors or system failures
options.D: They prevent the risk of unreadable handwriting and lost notes

explanation: Digital entries are clear, typed, and easily accessible across shifts, solving the problem of poor handwriting and misplaced paper charts. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h1)

question: A nurse asks an assistant to give a bed bath, and later checks on the patient to see if they are comfortable. What step of delegation is this?

options.A: Initial task assessment
options.B: Scope of practice expansion
options.C: Care plan formulation
options.D: Supervision and evaluation

explanation: Checking back on the patient and reviewing how the task was done completes the supervision and evaluation loop! [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h6)

question: Which component of the chain of infection is an infected human wound considered?

options.A: A natural vector
options.B: A portal of exit
options.C: A susceptible host
options.D: An infectious agent

explanation: An open wound serves as a portal of exit because it is a pathway for pathogens to leave the reservoir body. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T6#GNS313_U1_T6_h2)

question: Which group of people usually needs to visit the hospital or clinic the most?

options.A: Teens living in rural villages
options.B: Teenagers in secondary schools
options.C: Healthy young adults working jobs
options.D: Older adults and young children

explanation: Great thinking! The very young and our elderly grandparents have bodies that are more delicate against infections, so they tend to need healthcare services more frequently. [learn more](GST322_U1_T3#GST322_U1_T3_h2)

question: During a mental check, which sign is most typical for a patient with moderate to severe anxiety?

options.A: Flat affect and delayed motor movements
options.B: Delusions of grandeur and unresponsiveness
options.C: Profound lethargy and deep sleepiness
options.D: Rapid speech and poor ability to concentrate

explanation: When anxiety is high, the brain is racing! Patients often talk fast, jump between thoughts, and find it really hard to focus on questions. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T5#GNS314_U2_T5_h5)

question: Roughly what percentage of raw sewage is actually water?

options.A: Roughly 99.9 percent
options.B: Less than 10 percent
options.C: Around 75 percent
options.D: Exactly 50 percent

explanation: It might surprise you, but raw sewage is almost entirely water—about 99.9%! The solid waste makes up only a tiny fraction of what flows through the pipes. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h2)

question: A patient comes in with a severe pain crisis, but their oxygen saturation is completely normal at 98% on room air. What should you do about oxygen therapy?

options.A: Administer high-flow oxygen immediately to reverse the bone pain
options.B: Place the patient on a non-rebreather mask to prevent acute chest syndrome
options.C: Monitor saturation closely and withhold oxygen unless desaturation occurs
options.D: Apply nasal cannula oxygen only during periods of sleep

explanation: If their oxygen level is fine, extra oxygen isn't needed—in fact, it can trick the bone marrow into slowing down red blood cell production. Just keep a close eye on them! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T8#GNS313_U3_T8_h5)

question: What is another common name for primary polycythaemia?

options.A: Polycythaemia vera
options.B: Secondary erythrocytosis
options.C: Iron deficiency anemia
options.D: Aplastic anemia

explanation: Primary polycythaemia is also called polycythaemia vera. It happens right inside the bone marrow stem cells! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T8#GNS311_U2_T8_h2)

question: Unlike in wealthy nations where older women are mostly affected, what is the typical age group for breast cancer in Nigeria?

options.A: Younger women between thirty-five and fifty years
options.B: Elderly women over the age of eighty years
options.C: Adolescent girls during puberty
options.D: Infants with congenital genetic mutations

explanation: You'll often see breast cancer diagnosed in younger women here in Nigeria, unlike the older postmenopausal pattern seen in high-income countries. Keep this in mind during community postings! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h1)

question: What exactly is a windshield survey in community health?

options.A: Interviewing automobile drivers about local road accidents
options.B: Inspecting vehicles used for transporting emergency patients
options.C: Observing community conditions firsthand while moving through the area
options.D: Testing the window glass quality of local health clinics

explanation: Imagine driving or walking slowly through a neighborhood, looking at housing, open drainage, and market areas with your own eyes. That's a windshield survey! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h4)

question: Which symptom is a classic warning sign of dangerous preeclampsia getting worse?

options.A: Complete inability to swallow liquids
options.B: Severe frontal headache and hyperreflexia
options.C: Total loss of hearing in both ears
options.D: Sudden uncontrollable shaking of the feet

explanation: Always look out for this in clinicals! Brain irritation from high blood pressure and swelling often shows up as a bad headache and jumpy reflexes. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T6#GNS121_U7_T6_h5)

question: Why must you check the literacy level of a community before choosing your IEC materials?

options.A: To decide which doctor will be assigned to lead the surgical ward
options.B: To calculate the exact financial budget required for the health outreach program
options.C: To determine how many textbooks need to be ordered for the local primary school
options.D: To ensure the community can actually read and understand written text if print is used

explanation: If a community struggles with reading, handing out text-heavy brochures won't work well. You'll want to use pictures, audio, or drama instead! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T5#GNS124_U5_T5_h6)

question: When is a closed-ended question most helpful during an assessment?

options.A: When starting the orientation phase of an admission
options.B: When you need a quick, specific fact like a drug allergy
options.C: When you want the patient to describe their life story
options.D: When the patient is feeling anxious and needs to vent

explanation: Correct! Closed questions are great when you just need quick, straight-to-the-point facts like dates, numbers, or allergies. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h4)

question: In radiation safety, what does the golden rule acronym 'ALARA' stand for?

options.A: Always Limit All Radiologic Assessments
options.B: Absolute Limitation Of Radiation Angles
options.C: Avoid Lower Area Radiation Accidents
options.D: As Low As Reasonably Achievable

explanation: ALARA is a core safety mindset in healthcare: keep radiation doses As Low As Reasonably Achievable using shields, distance, and time. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T5#GNS222_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the underlying cause of Sheehan syndrome after severe childbirth bleeding?

options.A: Lack of blood supply causing pituitary gland tissue death
options.B: A severe kidney infection spreading from the uterus

question: Which of these is an early physical sign that an infant is becoming dehydrated?

options.C: Desire to increase overall patient hospital stays

question: Why is it dangerous to stuff a sharps box until it is completely filled to the brim?

question: What is the main reason for monitoring quality indicators in subacute care?

question: As a psychiatric nurse, how should you view a patient's mental health symptoms when you first meet them?

options.C: As an attempt by the psyche to protect itself

question: How should you document an adverse event in the patient's clinical chart?
